BGR 三因子模型的十二月残差波动

Intraday VWAP-deviation reversion with the horizon aligned to the 12-bar target. The 5m deviation of adjusted close from adjusted VWAP is standardized over the same 12 bars, so the signal measures a one-hour dislocation from fair value. Reversal is bet on that dislocation. Normalizing by monthly volatility-of-volatility, rather than one-day realized volatility, shrinks exposure when the volatility regime is unstable, where short-term reversion is less dependable.

Multi-day overextension reversion. The deviation of the daily adjusted close from the daily adjusted VWAP is standardized over 20 trading days and reversed. Anchoring to the daily fair-value level, rather than intraday VWAP, targets multi-day overextension where inventory-driven imbalances are more likely to correct over the next several bars.

Subtracting the same-timestamp cross-sectional mean removes market-wide moves, so the signal captures product-specific dislocations from VWAP. Idiosyncratic dislocations in futures are more likely to mean-revert than common commodity-wide shocks, which can persist as trends. Negating the time-series z-score of the demeaned deviation bets on reversion to the product's own VWAP.

Short-horizon VWAP reversion is combined with a term-structure carry signal. Products trading below VWAP with a high 12-month average basis (steeper backwardation) are favored, since hedging pressure and carry can reinforce reversion. Cross-sectional standardization of both legs keeps the combined score comparable across products.

Volatility-scaled intraday time-series momentum. Four-hour returns on completed 60-minute bars capture short-horizon trend persistence in futures, driven by slow hedging and order-flow execution. Dividing by trailing 60-minute return volatility stops high-volatility products from dominating the cross-section, and winsorizing limits the effect of outlier prints.

Incremental price-positioning coupling. Correlating 30-minute price changes with 30-minute open interest changes over 48 bars measures whether price moves coincide with new position building, not whether price and open interest co-trend in levels. Positive coupling suggests that moves are backed by new capital and are more likely to persist. Negative coupling suggests that moves are driven by position unwinding, which tends to fade.

expression: CLIP(CS_ZSCORE(IF_THEN_ELSE(TS_ANY(LT(ABS(DIVIDE(SUBTRACT(DIVIDE($adj_close, $adj_vwap), 1.0), TS_STD(RETURN($adj_close, 1.0), 80.0))), 0.5), 20.0), MULTIPLY(MULTIPLY(SIGN(DIVIDE(SUBTRACT(DIVIDE($adj_close, $adj_vwap), 1.0), TS_STD(RETURN($adj_close, 1.0), 80.0))), MAX(SUBTRACT(ABS(DIVIDE(SUBTRACT(DIVIDE($adj_close, $adj_vwap), 1.0), TS_STD(RETURN($adj_close, 1.0), 80.0))), TS_MIN(ABS(DIVIDE(SUBTRACT(DIVIDE($adj_close, $adj_vwap), 1.0), TS_STD(RETURN($adj_close, 1.0), 80.0))), 20.0)), 0.0)), MULTIPLY(ADD(1.0, MAX(DIVIDE(SUBTRACT($adj_close, DELAY(TS_MAX($adj_high, 80.0), 1.0)), TS_STD(RETURN($adj_close, 1.0), 80.0)), 0.0)), DIVIDE(SUBTRACT($adj_close, TS_MIN($adj_low, 80.0)), SUBTRACT(TS_MAX($adj_high, 80.0), TS_MIN($adj_low, 80.0))))), 0.0)), -2.0, 2.0)
description: Within each product, price that recently touched adjusted VWAP and then moves away from it tends to continue in the direction of the departure. The effect is stronger when the close sits near the upper part of its channel and when the break beyond the prior channel upper is deep relative to recent volatility. Each signal is ranked and standardized across instruments at each timestamp, then clipped to a bounded range.

When the rolling VWAP equilibrium changes slope direction, instruments are more likely to rotate back toward their own moving-average equilibrium. The signal is a cross-sectionally ranked, negated standardized distance from the moving average, weighted by how often VWAP slope turns occur in the lookback window. Windows are in native 5m bars and scale with the period.

When price is at a relative high or low within its recent range but short-horizon momentum fails to confirm that position, the divergence is ranked across the product panel at each timestamp. The signal is taken only while adjusted close sits between adjusted VWAP and the prior daily close, so only one anchor has been crossed. Because the event is read as a reversal, the final score is the negated standardized divergence rank, so stronger unconfirmed highs score lower and unconfirmed lows score higher.

Cross-sectionally, products whose path efficiency (net displacement over path length) is improving most strongly, in the direction of their net move, tend to continue in that direction when price sits near its equilibrium reference (VWAP). The event signal decays linearly over the same window, so older events carry less weight.

expression: CLIP(CS_ZSCORE(MULTIPLY(MULTIPLY(MAX(SUBTRACT(DIVIDE(ABS(SUBTRACT($adj_close, DELAY($adj_close, 80.0))), TS_SUM(ABS(DELTA($adj_close, 1.0)), 80.0)), TS_MEAN(DIVIDE(ABS(SUBTRACT($adj_close, DELAY($adj_close, 80.0))), TS_SUM(ABS(DELTA($adj_close, 1.0)), 80.0)), 80.0)), 0.0), DIVIDE(ABS(SUBTRACT($adj_close, DELAY($adj_close, 80.0))), TS_SUM(ABS(DELTA($adj_close, 1.0)), 80.0))), MULTIPLY(SUBTRACT(0.5, DIVIDE(SUBTRACT($adj_close, TS_MIN($adj_low, 80.0)), SUBTRACT(TS_MAX($adj_high, 80.0), TS_MIN($adj_low, 80.0)))), DIVIDE($volume, TS_MEAN($volume, 80.0))))), -3.0, 3.0)
description: On 5m bars, when path efficiency (net displacement over path length) expands above its own recent average, the move is a range-oscillation event. Price is expected to rotate back toward the channel center, so the signal fades positions near the channel upper boundary and favors the lower side. Volume ratio confirms participation, and the cross-sectional z-score is clipped to [-3, 3].

expression: CLIP(MULTIPLY(MULTIPLY(MULTIPLY(IF_THEN_ELSE(AND(GT($adj_close, MIN($adj_vwap, $adj_close@1d)), LT($adj_close, MAX($adj_vwap, $adj_close@1d))), 1.0, 0.0), NEG(SIGN(SUBTRACT($adj_close, MULTIPLY(ADD($adj_vwap, $adj_close@1d), 0.5))))), CS_DEMEAN(CS_RANK(ABS(DIVIDE(DIVIDE(SUBTRACT($adj_close, $adj_close@1d), $adj_close@1d), TS_STD(RETURN($adj_close, 1.0), 20.0)))))), MULTIPLY(ADD(1.0, CLIP(NEG(LOG(DIVIDE(TS_MEAN(SUBTRACT($adj_high, $adj_low), 5.0), TS_MEAN(SUBTRACT($adj_high, $adj_low), 20.0)))), -1.0, 1.0)), CS_RANK(DIVIDE(ABS(SUBTRACT($adj_close, $adj_vwap)), MULTIPLY($adj_close, TS_STD(RETURN($adj_close, 1.0), 20.0)))))), -2.0, 2.0)
description: Inside the VWAP-prior close interstitial zone, price rotates back toward the zone equilibrium. The rotation is stronger when the stock's prior-close deviation, scaled by its own volatility, ranks high cross-sectionally, when the pre-event range is compressing, and when the break depth from VWAP ranks high cross-sectionally.

expression: CLIP(CS_ZSCORE(MULTIPLY(IF_THEN_ELSE(OR(TS_ANY(NE(SIGN(SUBTRACT(DIVIDE($adj_close, $adj_vwap), 1.0)), DELAY(SIGN(SUBTRACT(DIVIDE($adj_close, $adj_vwap), 1.0)), 1.0)), 20.0), TS_ANY(LT(ABS(SUBTRACT(DIVIDE($adj_close, $adj_vwap), 1.0)), TS_STD(SUBTRACT(DIVIDE($adj_close, $adj_vwap), 1.0), 20.0)), 20.0)), TS_ZSCORE(SUBTRACT(DIVIDE($adj_close, $adj_vwap), 1.0), 20.0), 0.0), MULTIPLY(CLIP(SUBTRACT(1.0, ABS(DIVIDE(SUBTRACT(MULTIPLY(2.0, $adj_close), ADD(TS_MAX($adj_high, 20.0), TS_MIN($adj_low, 20.0))), SUBTRACT(TS_MAX($adj_high, 20.0), TS_MIN($adj_low, 20.0))))), 0.0, 1.0), ADD(0.5, CLIP(SUBTRACT(1.0, DIVIDE($volume, TS_MEAN($volume, 20.0))), 0.0, 1.0))))), -3.0, 3.0)
description: After price contacts VWAP and then reclaims it or fails to cross it and moves away, the continuation direction given by the adjusted close's signed deviation from adjusted VWAP tends to persist. The signal is strongest when price sits near the midpoint of its recent range and when volume does not confirm the move. Volume non-confirmation is used as a weighting term, with a 0.5 floor so that the signal is not fully gated off. Each period scales all windows and the touch threshold from the primary period.

expression: IF_THEN_ELSE(TS_ANY(AND(AND(AND(GT(TS_ZSCORE(DIVIDE(ABS(DELTA($adj_close, 20.0)), TS_SUM(ABS(DELTA($adj_close, 1.0)), 20.0)), 80.0), 1.0), GT(DELTA(DIVIDE(ABS(DELTA($adj_close, 20.0)), TS_SUM(ABS(DELTA($adj_close, 1.0)), 20.0)), 20.0), 0.0)), GT(DIVIDE(SUBTRACT($adj_high, $adj_low), TS_MEAN(SUBTRACT($adj_high, $adj_low), 80.0)), 1.0)), LE(ABS(DIVIDE(DIVIDE(SUBTRACT($adj_open, DELAY($adj_close, 1.0)), DELAY($adj_close, 1.0)), TS_STD(RETURN($adj_close, 1.0), 80.0))), 4.0)), 20.0), NEG(SUBTRACT(CS_RANK(DIVIDE(SUBTRACT($adj_close, TS_MIN($adj_close, 80.0)), SUBTRACT(TS_MAX($adj_close, 80.0), TS_MIN($adj_close, 80.0)))), 0.5)), 0.0)
description: A trend acceleration burst (path efficiency z-score rising with positive efficiency momentum), confirmed by range expansion and passing a robust opening-gap filter, marks an overextended move. Under range-oscillation guidance, price is expected to rotate back toward equilibrium, so the alpha fades the cross-sectional range-position extreme. The signal persists while the gated condition remains valid within the recent window and returns to 0 once it expires.

expression: MULTIPLY(IF_THEN_ELSE(LE(DIVIDE(TS_MEAN(SUBTRACT($adj_high, $adj_low), 5.0), TS_MEAN(SUBTRACT($adj_high, $adj_low), 20.0)), 1.0), IF_THEN_ELSE(TS_ANY(GE(DIVIDE(SUBTRACT($adj_close, MIN(TS_MIN($adj_low, 20.0), $adj_close@1d)), SUBTRACT(MAX(TS_MAX($adj_high, 20.0), $adj_close@1d), MIN(TS_MIN($adj_low, 20.0), $adj_close@1d))), 0.9), 20.0), -1.0, IF_THEN_ELSE(TS_ANY(LE(DIVIDE(SUBTRACT($adj_close, MIN(TS_MIN($adj_low, 20.0), $adj_close@1d)), SUBTRACT(MAX(TS_MAX($adj_high, 20.0), $adj_close@1d), MIN(TS_MIN($adj_low, 20.0), $adj_close@1d))), 0.1), 20.0), 1.0, 0.0)), 0.0), CS_RANK(DIVIDE(ABS(SUBTRACT($adj_close, $adj_close@1d)), SUBTRACT(MAX(TS_MAX($adj_high, 20.0), $adj_close@1d), MIN(TS_MIN($adj_low, 20.0), $adj_close@1d)))))
description: Closes at the extreme top or bottom of a rolling range anchored to the prior daily close tend to rotate back toward the reference space, so the signal fades the extreme. The fade is gated to bars where the range is not expanding, and it is weighted by the cross-sectional rank of each product's departure from its prior close. The signal persists while the extreme condition remains valid within the window and expires afterward.
